atoms.b:
Crime & Death penalty
The USA is seen as a country with ((high)) crime rates. However, crime rates ((decreased)) from 1992 to 2022, although some types of violent and property ((crime)) increased, especially in the Southern states. Even so, crime ((rates)) are still much higher in the USA than in Europe.

There are different forms of punishment for criminals. The USA is the only ((Western)) democracy where the death penalty is ((legal)), being legal in 27 of its 50 states. The frequency of executions depends on federal ((government)) — for example, Joe Biden was against the death penalty and changed a lot of death penalty sentences to life in ((prison)).

instruction.text: Read the historical events about the death penalty and put them in chronological order.

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>BCE</lang> steht für <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>before common era</lang> und bedeutet vor Christus.
hint.label: BCE

atoms.text: The first death penalty laws were introduced in the 18th century BCE in ancient Babylon.
Britain strongly influenced America’s use of the death penalty. European settlers brought capital punishment to the colonies, and the first recorded execution was in Jamestown, Virginia, in 1608.
Some states began abolishing the death penalty or reducing the number of executions in the 19th century.
In the 1960s, it was argued that the death penalty was a “cruel and unusual” punishment.
In 1972, the Supreme Court suspended the death penalty because existing laws were found to be unconstitutional.
In 1976, the Supreme Court accepted some reforms, so states that wanted to bring back the death penalty included these reforms in their new laws.
To this day, the USA has retained the death penalty, but established some limitations
